quandoUsar: Confirm an action that succeeded and asks nothing more: draft saved, link copied, invitation sent.
A single notice at a time, in a place you control, with `open` and `onOpenChange` tied to the screen's state.
Touch screens where swiping the notice sideways is the natural way to dismiss it.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast-action` when the notice offers undo or another action; its timer pauses on mouse and focus.
Use `toast-stack` for several notices in a row or of different types (error, warning, loading); this one only shows the success checkmark.
Use `alert` for errors and warnings that must stay on screen until the user acts.
acessibilidade: It is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic`: the screen reader reads title and description together, without interrupting, and the outgoing copies are hidden.
The timer does not pause on mouse or focus and there is no shortcut to reach the notice; do not put anything in it that the user needs to read carefully or act on.
The close button is a `<button>` with `aria-label` “Dismiss notification”, fixed in English in the file.
movimento: It enters rising 16 px from a slightly smaller scale, with a no-overshoot spring, while the checkmark draws itself; on closing, it drops a little and fades.
When dragged sideways, it follows the finger; past 80 px or released quickly, it flies off in the direction of the gesture at the release velocity, otherwise it springs back.
With “reduce motion”, entrance and exit become a short fade and dragging is turned off.
responsivo: The width goes up to 26 rem and fits the parent; the title stays on one line and is truncated with an ellipsis, so put long details in `description`, which wraps.
notasIA: Import the default: `import Toast from "@/components/ryan-ui/toast/toast"` (there is no named export). It appears where it is rendered; position it yourself, for example in a fixed container in the corner.

Automatic closing (`duration`, default 4500 ms) only works with `onOpenChange`; pass a stable function, such as the `setOpen` from `useState`, because a new function on every render restarts the countdown.
To show the notice again, set `open` back to `true`; changing `title` while it is open swaps the text in place, without restarting the timer.
